security_spec.violation_condition: QEMU implements the Smnip CSRs at the old (incorrect) CSR addresses from the pre-fix spec, specifically mithreshold at 0xFB1 (which overlaps the debug trigger CSR address range 0x7A0-0x7BF) and sithreshold at 0x1B1 (non-standard offset), instead of the corrected contiguous block at M-mode 0x346-0x349 / S-mode 0x146-0x149.
security_spec.summary: Pre-fix mithreshold CSR at 0xFB1 lands in M-mode debug trigger CSR address space (0x7A0-0x7BF); a guest write to mithreshold at 0xFB1 would alias to debug trigger registers, allowing unprivileged interrupt-priority manipulation to corrupt M-mode debug state or vice versa — a CSR address collision enabling cross-privilege state corruption.

findings.finding: Smnip CSRs (mithreshold, mnxti, mscontext, sithreshold, snxti, sscontext) are not registered in the CSR table at any address — neither at the old incorrect addresses 0xFB1/0x1B1 nor at the new correct addresses 0x346-0x349/0x146-0x149. No CSR address collision or privilege escape is possible.

Only RNMI CSR addresses are defined (0x740-0x744). No Smnip CSR macros (CSR_MITHRE, CSR_MNXTI, CSR_MSCONTEXT, CSR_SITHRE, CSR_SNXTI, CSR_SSCONTEXT) exist at any address. The debug trigger range 0x7A0-0x7BF is cleanly used only for debug/trace CSRs.

CPU state struct contains only RNMI fields (mnscratch, mnepc, mncause) and mcontext (debug). No Smnip-specific state variables (e.g., mithreshold, mnxti, mscontext) exist. No old or wrong semantics in use.

Only mnret instruction translation exists (gated by REQUIRE_SMRNMI). No Smnip-specific instruction translation (e.g., mnret.nxti sequence patterns or CSR read/write helpers for Smnip CSRs) is present.
ext_smrnmi is explicitly force-disabled at CPU finalize time due to OpenSBI compatibility, so even the base RNMI extension is not functional in practice. No Smnip vulnerability surface exists.
